verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four runs are measured before the coolant was switched: run One was "switched 4 May" yet "ran 6 minutes shorter by 29 March", and run Three was "switched 5 October" yet measured "by 30 September". The other two runs (3 June/27 June, 2 November/26 November) show the intended ~3-week window, so the improvement in One and Three is dated before the intervention existed.

The numbers cover a narrower population than the claim: "Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol" while "a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol", so the 6-11 percent drops are computed on a self-selected fully-compliant 75% and compared against a prior quarter that included everyone, rather than on the ward infection rate the claim is about.

"Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices" but "about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices", so the 4-7 percent gains are measured on a selected 80% of orders (the higher-priced ones) and compared to a month earlier when all orders counted — that is not revenue per order for the line.

A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Outdoor temperature in each cohort's city fell ten degrees from the month before, and every cohort slept in unconditioned rooms open to outside air", so all four cohorts were sleeping in materially cooler rooms across the exact measurement window, and cooler sleeping temperature lowers resting heart rate on its own.
